report:
The study reveals normal knee joint alignment.  No fracture or bone contusion is noted.     
  There is loss of signal of the proximal ACL with deformed residual distal part.   Normal PCL with 0 ligament fiber is observed.  No anterior tibial translation is seen.  
  
    Thinning medial meniscus with blunting small size of anterior and posterior horn and displaced meniscal fragment located along intercondylar region causing "Double PCL sign", represent  
 bucket handle tear of medial meniscus.       Mild hyperintense deep proximal MCL is noted.   
  
   Mild thinning articular cartilage at weight bearing site of the medial femoral condyle, no cartilagenous defect is noted.  
  
   Thickened hyperintense proximal FCL, suggesting FCL sprain.   Intrasubstance tear proximal popliteus tendon is noted.  Biceps femoris tendon is preserved.   Lateral meiniscus is not torn. 
  
   Mild thinning articular cartilage of the medial and lateral femoral condyle, and tibial plateau. 
 NO cartilagenous defect is noted.  
  
  Normal PF joint alignment 
  Focal delamination with hyperintense overlying cartilage, about 5mm., at mid medial patellar facet is noted. No subchondral bone lesion is seen.  
 Moderate joint effusion with fluid along suprapatellar bursa is seen.  Mild thickened synovial tissue is  observed.  
  Quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact 
  Mild lobulated cystic lesions at  infrapatellar and posterolateral and posteromedial joint capsule, should be small synovial cysts.   Complete tear of ACL,   
   Bucket handle tear of the medial meniscus. 
   Mild proximal MCL sprain 
  Proximal FCL sprain  
  Intra substance tear proximal popliteus tendon 
    PF ;  delamination with hyperintense overlying cartilage, about 5mm., at mid medial patellar facet 
    Chronic PF synovitis with suprapatellar bursitis 
and small synovial cysts

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Síndrome meniscal medial rodilla derecha.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
El menisco lateral es de morfología y señal conservada, sin signos de una rotura categórica.
Rotura compleja del cuerno posterior y cuerpo del menisco medial con segmento que se insinúa de manera
parcial al receso menisco tibial con edema de las partes blandas regionales.
Finas úlceras condrales de espesor parcial de la región central de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral
medial. El resto de los cartílagos femorotibiales y de la tróclea femoral sin alteraciones. Úlceras condrales
de espesor total del vértice y faceta medial de la rótula con cambios óseos secundarios.
Mínimo derrame articular. No hay quistes poplíteos patológicos.
Aumento de señal de la inserción distal del tendón cuadricipital y de la inserción proximal del tendón
rotuliano, sin signos de rotura. Edema del tejido celular subcutáneo del aspecto anterior de la rodilla con
laminar cantidad de líquido regional.
Tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.
Impresión:
Rotura del menisco medial con segmento que se insinúa al receso menisco tibial con edema las partes
blandas regionales.
Condropatía lesiones grado 2 de la región central de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral medial.
Condropatía lesiones grado 4 de la rótula.
Mínimo derrame articular.
Leve tendinosis cuadricipital distal y rotuliana proximal.
Edema del tejido celular subcutáneo del aspecto anterior de la rodilla con laminar cantidad de líquido
regional

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: A few days of anterior/medial knee pain.
Comparison: [REDACTED].

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion with synovitis. No intra-articular bodies. Small, ruptured Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex tear of the posterior horn/body with a small flap formation migrating into the lateral meniscotibial gutter. Minimal peripheral extrusion of the body segment. Root attachments are intact.
Medial compartment cartilage: Thinning of the weightbearing femoral condyle cartilage, without focal defect. Tibial cartilage is maintained.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Fraying of the body segment inner margin.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Patellar cartilage is maintained. Focal full-thickness fissuring along the medial/central trochlea with underlying subchondral cystic change.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Chronic partial tear of the proximal fibers.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Intact, with periligamentous edema likely related to medial meniscal pathology.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 10 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Complex tear of the medial meniscus.
2.	Inner margin fraying of the lateral meniscal body.
3.	Chronic partial tear of the ACL.
4.	Mild medial and patellofemoral chondrosis.
5.	Small knee effusion with synovitis.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Gonalgia izquierda
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones en significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales sin lesiones significativas.
Aumento de señal central del cuerno posterior y parte del cuerpo del menisco medial que
impresiona contactar de manera periférica la superficie articular inferior, que puede representar
una pequeña rotura, no desplazada. Discreto edema de las partes blandas perimeniscales.
El menisco lateral es de morfología y señal conservada, sin signos de rotura.
Cartílagos de los compartimentos femorotibiales sin alteraciones.
Úlceras condrales de espesor total con cambios óseos secundarios de distribución difusa de la
articulación patelofemoral.
Leve derrame articular. No hay quistes poplíteos patológicos.
Tendones cuadricipital, rotuliano, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial
dentro de límites normales.
Impresión:
Signos sugerentes de una rotura periférica del menisco medial con edema de las partes blandas
regionales, correlacionar con clínica.
Condropatía lesiones grado 4 de la articulación patelofemoral.
Leve derrame articular

Técnica: RMN de la rodilla. Resultados: lesión focal de la superficie condral del cóndilo lateral. Impresión: lesión condral del cóndilo lateral.

Findings:  Moderate knee joint effusion. 6 mm intra-articular body posterior to the tibial attachment of the PCL.  No sinister bone marrow changes. Small intraosseous ganglion cyst adjacent to the tibial attachment of the PCL. Intact ACL and PCL.  Mild thickening of the proximal MCL in keeping with previous injury and healing with scarring. Intact LCL.  On a background of mucoid degeneration there is a complex tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with an associated 13 mm 16 mm x 7 mm parameniscal cyst posteriorly. Minor bone stress changes in the posterior aspect of the medial tibial condyle however no discrete fracture. Intact lateral meniscus.  Normal appearance of the pes anserine tendons, popliteus tendon, distal biceps femoris tendon and distal iliotibial band.  Focal high-grade chondral fissuring along the lateral femoral trochlear surface with minor underlying bone stress change. Otherwise well-maintained tricompartmental hyaline cartilage.  
Conclusion: On a background of mucoid degeneration there is a complex tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with an associated 13 mm 16 mm x 7 mm parameniscal cyst posteriorly. Minor bone stress changes in the posterior aspect of the medial tibial condyle however no discrete fracture. Ancillary findings described above.
